findings.failure_path: Round A is accepted using controller version A and records its candidate hash; a later legitimate round changes the freeze algorithm to version B; promotion loads version B for Round A, recomputes a different hash, finds no matching ledger, and refuses an otherwise fully bound automatic-merge chain. This contradicts the acceptance guarantee for ledgers accepted at their own bases.
findings.smallest_fix: Make candidate freezing versioned and backward-compatible: have the landing-owned controller recompute the ledger's recorded freeze version, then add a regression where the controller changes after an accepted round.

findings.failure_path: `git worktree add` can create its administrative registration or checkout directory and then return nonzero. This branch only runs unchecked `shutil.rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)` and never removes or verifies the registration, so failed runs can leak repository worktree state and silently leave a directory.
findings.smallest_fix: On add failure, inspect the worktree registry, perform targeted removal when this path was registered, verify both registry absence and directory deletion, and include any cleanup failure in the reported error.

concern_results.conclusion: Controller drift breaks the required historical-round guarantee: every old ledger may remain valid at its own base, yet recomputation with the landing controller can produce a different candidate hash and refuse the promotion. The diff tests validator drift but not controller-freeze drift.

The merge-shape and 64-step checks are present, but detached-checkout containment is incomplete when `git worktree add` fails after creating state: cleanup is unverified and may leave both a registration and directory.

challenge_focus: Succession over the fix batch: the historical round is now judged with the landing tree controller and validator, the detached checkout release is verified with no repository-wide prune, and the walk bound is exact. Hunt for what those fixes introduce or leave open: a landing tree whose own validator or controller is hollowed or whose freeze differs from the one that minted an old ledger, a release check that can be satisfied while a registration or directory survives, an error path that still prints ok or hides the refusal reason, a boundary chain that is accepted or refused off by one, and any regression in the pre-existing single-ledger and manifest verdicts or their output tokens.
predecessor_challenge_focuses: Bypass the new first-parent chain accept path: construct a promotion HEAD whose every step passes the automatic-merge tree equality and the sync/round classification yet lands content no round reviewed (evil second parents, merges of ancestors, re-merged old heads, octopus or shallow histories, a round whose evidence directory or validator is forged inside its own branch), abuse of the detached temporary checkout (path, cleanup, symlinks, untracked files, concurrent runs), and any way the name-level coverage check or the sync classification can be satisfied while unreviewed bytes reach the target.
